ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before adjudication. It says what a `Ruling:` line must contain and what "work" and "parked" each trigger.
ACTION: Read `.sdd/12-tide-cache/progress.md` (the ledger). Confirm Tasks 1 to 4 are complete and list every finding still open on Task 5.
ACTION: Read the Task 5 section of `specs/plans/12-tide-cache.md` and the round-5 re-review report in `.sdd/12-tide-cache/`. Check whether the spec requires `tide/parse.py` to reject a negative interval when the header line is missing.
ACTION: Append one `Ruling:` line for F2 to the ledger, as work or parked with my reason, in the form `fix-loop.md` gives.

Message to partner:

Task 5 (parse tide-table headers) has used all five fix attempts. One Important finding is still open. I call it F2: `tide/parse.py` still accepts a negative interval when the header line is missing.

I will not dispatch a sixth fix round. The five-attempt cap means I must now adjudicate. I am reading the fix-loop reference and the Task 5 spec text. Then I will write a ruling for F2 in the ledger. The ruling records F2 either as work to do or as parked, with my reason.

I will not mark Task 5 complete until the ruling is written. I will report the ruling to you when it is done, and I will continue the plan from there.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The cap is a circuit breaker. If five targeted fixes do not close one finding, a sixth attempt of the same kind rarely helps. A decision about the finding itself is more useful, such as a changed approach, a spec clarification, or a recorded deferral.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
